assessment.body:
Friday 6:00 PM IST. Day 70. The satellite has spoken. The Omani lane is gone.

THE NASA SATELLITE FINDING — WHAT IT MEANS
Dr Y Nithiyanandam (@prof_nithiya, 9:16 AM May 8): "NASA satellites picked up multiple fire signatures, right on the Strait of Hormuz separation zone. Multiple ships moving near Omani waters appeared to be hit. The area is now completely deserted — zero traffic. It appears that Iran is attempting to block the old route through Omani waters to prevent ships from bypassing their tolls."

This is the definitive geospatial confirmation of Iran's Hormuz strategy.

THE COMPLETE CORRIDOR ELIMINATION — CONFIRMED
• Omani water lane (traditional route): NASA fire signatures — deserted, zero traffic
• Hormuz Traffic Separation Zone southern side: active kinetic attack zone
• Fujairah bypass (UAE side): Iranian drone attack May 5 — fire, 3 Indians wounded
• Musandam peninsula (Oman territory): residential building struck
• IRGC northern lane: the ONLY remaining corridor — requires toll and coordination
Every bypass has been eliminated. The architecture is complete.

THE INSTITUTIONAL PERMANENCE
• Iran formalised a government IRGC vetting agency — not ad-hoc, permanent
• Northward rerouting map issued — the legal architecture
• NASA fire signatures — the kinetic enforcement
• Together: a permanent Hormuz control system that will outlast this war

THE KHAMENEI FACTOR
• Pezeshkian confirmed 2+ hour in-person meeting with Mojtaba Khamenei
• First confirmed direct Supreme Leader engagement since February 28
• Khamenei "playing key role in overseeing negotiations"
• The decision-maker is at the table — this is positive for deal prospects
• But any deal must now accommodate Iran's permanent Hormuz control architecture

INDIA'S REALITY AT DAY 70
• Zero uncontested routing — confirmed by NASA satellite
• IRGC toll system is the only active corridor
• MEA must decide this weekend: engage toll system or wait for deal
• Kharif fertiliser: May 10-12 sourcing deadline
• Brent $101 — OMC hike risk returning at Rs 2-4/L
• Murkowski AUMF May 11 = deal pressure this weekend

VERDICT: The geospatial assessment is complete. Iran has built — and is kinetically enforcing — a permanent Hormuz control architecture. The satellite evidence removes all remaining ambiguity. The negotiation is not about reopening Hormuz. It is about who controls it, under what institutional framework, at what cost to passing vessels, and on whose legal authority. India wakes up Saturday with zero uncontested routing and a kharif fertiliser sourcing deadline. The decisions made in New Delhi, Islamabad, and Tehran this weekend will determine India's energy and food security for the rest of 2026.
